builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Sparse Convolution
summary: This method replaces standard dense convolution with a direct sparse convolution algorithm designed to exploit high weight sparsity resulting from pruning. It requires implementing custom sparse kernels and handling irregular memory access patterns, which increases engineering complexity compared to using standard dense libraries. Adoption can fail if the model's sparsity is too low or unstructured, as the overhead of sparse indexing may negate the computational savings, or if existing vendor libraries already optimize the specific workload effectively.
rationale: While the speedups are relevant for edge deployment, the results are preliminary and achieving them likely requires custom kernel engineering effort that may exceed the resources of a small team unless a maintained library becomes available.
technique: Direct Sparse Convolution for Pruned Kernels

claims.statement: This method replaces standard dense convolution with a direct sparse convolution algorithm designed to exploit high weight sparsity resulting from pruning. It requires implementing custom sparse kernels and handling irregular memory access patterns, which increases engineering complexity compared to using standard dense libraries. Adoption can fail if the model's sparsity is too low or unstructured, as the overhead of sparse indexing may negate the computational savings, or if existing vendor libraries already optimize the specific workload effectively.
The authors report up to 1.65x speedup over dense convolution on NVIDIA A100 and up to 1.52x on Jetson Nano for high-sparsity 3x3 convolutions.
